clue.text: A row in the office?

parts.note: an office row is not a quarrel but a line of things, papers held in order or people standing one behind another

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bust-up has broken out at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts as an argument; it is a line, as in soldiers marching in single line, and the office is where papers are kept in one.
explanation.definitionFit: A file is a line of people one behind another, and also an office folder of papers.

clue.text: Move into lead and cast a bust?

definitions.meaning: to push to the front of a race or contest
to cast a bust is to make, as a smith does at the anvil, a sculpted head

explanation.surface: A sculptor pours metal into a mould, perhaps of lead, to make a portrait bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' and 'cast' suggest metalwork; the first sense is to pull in front, the second splits into making (by smithing) a sculpted head.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on and take the lead is to advance; making a head in metal is smithing one.

clue.text: Drinks may be, or shoes

definitions.meaning: a drink can be spiked with a dash of spirits
shoes are fastened with strings threaded through eyelets

explanation.surface: A list of things that might be tampered with or tied.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiked drinks have alcohol added; tied shoes have their strings done up.

clue.text: Pop-singers can be overpowering!

indicators.note: says the letters of the clue's pop-singers can be rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A complaint that pop stars can be too much to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges POPSINGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppressing someone means crushing or tyrannising them, overwhelming them.

clue.text: Litter container?

parts.note: not a bin for rubbish but a place holding a sow's litter of young

explanation.surface: A question about a rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' suggests rubbish; it is a brood of piglets.
explanation.definitionFit: A sty or farm unit where pigs, and so their young, are kept.

clue.text: Fish going in a circle may be off-balance

indicators.note: tells us the fish is placed inside the circle

parts.note: a ring is a circle
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish swimming round and round might lose its balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish going in a circle' reads as a picture of a swimming fish; 'going in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeling means staggering or swaying, unsteady on one's feet.

clue.text: Traded ring for outdated money in Italy

parts.note: sold means traded
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone sold a ring to raise some old Italian cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A soldo was a small Italian coin, long out of use.
explanation.definitionFit: The soldo was a former Italian copper coin, worth a twentieth of a lira.

clue.text: Audacious ring-leader held to be unwise

indicators.note: says one letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: impudent means audacious, cheeky

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bold gang boss is judged reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring-leader' is R, the first letter of 'ring', which IMPUDENT 'held' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means rash, lacking good judgement.

clue.text: Song causing merriment

explanation.surface: A tune that makes people laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee is an unaccompanied part-song, and the word also means joy.

clue.text: Publican getting rent-rise, about to swear

indicators.note: the turned word goes round the second piece
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to aver is to swear or declare

explanation.surface: A landlord facing a rent increase is about to curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns RENT to TNER, which goes 'about' AVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverner is an old word for one who keeps an inn or tavern.

clue.text: Shape of wreck, it's said, resting on seaweed

indicators.note: in an across clue, the first piece sits before the second
tells us the word wreck is said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: the clue's own word, heard aloud
tangle is a type of kelp, a seaweed

explanation.surface: A shipwreck lies on a bed of seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' signals a sound-alike of 'wreck'; 'resting on' places that before the seaweed. Tangle is a large brown kelp of northern shores.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblong, a four-sided figure with right angles, is a geometric shape.

clue.text: Slip up or slip by

explanation.surface: Two ways of slipping.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a small mistake, and time lapses when it passes.

clue.text: Clothe distressed English nude

indicators.note: distressed letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gets a naked Englishman dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges NUDE into NDUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is an old word meaning to dress or invest with garments.

clue.text: Peg EU oil production — that's the conclusion

indicators.note: signals the letters are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: Oil output across the European Union is pegged: final word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' rearranges PEGEUOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is the closing section of a book or play.

clue.text: Minute? Time's of no significance, solving the clue.

definitions.text: Minute? Time's of no significance, solving the clue.

parts.words: Minute? Time's of no significance, solving the clue.
parts.note: minute here is tiny, not sixty seconds, so time does not matter; the remark says the word means of no size at all

explanation.surface: A remark that a minute doesn't matter when you're busy solving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like sixty seconds; it is pronounced my-NEWT, very small.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeny-weeny is a childish phrase for very small, tiny.

clue.text: Painter of sporting activity around the north

indicators.note: says the sport goes round the other letter

parts.note: hockey is a sport
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An artist who paints sport somewhere in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: David Hockney is the English painter famous for pool scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: David Hockney is a celebrated British artist.

clue.text: The final disposal is promising

definitions.meaning: the consigning of a body to a grave or fire
pledging oneself, binding to a course

explanation.surface: A burial is described as hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: Committal is the act of consigning a body at a funeral, and of pledging or binding oneself.

clue.text: In a sylvan retreat you get an amorous glance

parts.note: a glade is a clearing in a wood
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: In a woodland clearing someone catches a flirtatious look.
explanation.walkthrough: To give someone the glad eye is to look at them with obvious desire.
explanation.definitionFit: The glad eye is a flirtatious, inviting look.

clue.text: A cunning ruse — one selects the initial characters? That's it!

definitions.text: A cunning ruse — one selects the initial characters? That's it!

indicators.note: tells the solver the thing described is the clue itself, so take the opening letter of each of its words

explanation.surface: A trick where someone picks out opening letters, and the clue proves it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of 'A Cunning Ruse One Selects The Initial Characters' spell the answer, and the clue describes the very device it uses.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a poem or puzzle in which the opening letters of lines spell a word.

clue.text: Takes pleasure in product of sire and dam

indicators.note: the offspring of the two words is their letters bred into a new order

explanation.surface: A breeder delights in the foal of a stallion and a mare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product of' rearranges SIRE and DAM together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who admires something enjoys or esteems it.

clue.text: Reveals distressed divers

indicators.note: distressed letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A news story uncovers scuba divers in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges REVEALS. 'divers' is the old word for various, not underwater swimmers.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers is an archaic adjective meaning various or sundry, so a number of.

clue.text: Quip about a girl being a prude?

indicators.note: the joke goes round the girl's name

parts.note: a pun is a wordplay quip
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A joke at a girl's expense paints her as straitlaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, not 'concerning'; the girl's name sits inside the quip.
explanation.definitionFit: A Puritan is one with strict moral views, a prig.

clue.text: Some reading for the journey?

explanation.surface: Someone picks a book to take on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is an extract from a text, and also a voyage by sea.

clue.text: Problems with delivery? Call for them!

definitions.text: Problems with delivery? Call for them!

parts.words: Problems with delivery? Call for them!
parts.note: not a parcel or speech going wrong but a difficult childbirth, for which these professionals are sent for

explanation.surface: A parcel hasn't turned up and someone says to phone the courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests the post; it is a baby's birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Midwives assist women in childbirth.

clue.text: Bereaved, but making marriage vow within two weeks

indicators.note: the vow sits inside the two weeks

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for week, so two weeks gives a pair of them
I do is what is said at the altar

explanation.surface: Someone loses a spouse within a fortnight of the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts I DO inside W W.
explanation.definitionFit: A widow is a woman who has lost her husband, so a bereaved person.

clue.text: Wages spiral?

definitions.meaning: a helical thread, as on a bolt

explanation.surface: A wage-price spiral.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw is old British slang for a wage.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is slang for a salary, and a screw has a helical thread.

clue.text: Anchor fouling nameless fish

indicators.note: a fouled anchor is tangled, so its letters are jumbled
N is the abbreviation for name, so the word loses it

explanation.surface: An anchor snags a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' drops N from ANCHOR to leave ACHOR, and 'fouling' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Small neat binding?

definitions.meaning: neat is an old word for cattle, so a small one is a young beast
a leather made from that young beast's hide, used to cover books

explanation.surface: A tidy little book cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' reads as tidy; it means cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cow, and a leather made from its skin used for book covers.

clue.text: Took part in a recording about Lawrence

indicators.note: the recording goes round the other piece

parts.note: CD stands for compact disc, a recording
T.E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Someone appeared in an audio piece about Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; T.E. Lawrence is regularly reduced to his initials in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting a part in a play or film means playing a role.

clue.text: Marine ate dog's dinner — put new life in him!

indicators.note: British slang for a mess, so the letters are made into a mess and rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier ate dog food, and needs reviving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog's dinner' (British slang for a mess) rearranges MARINEATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To revive means to bring back to life or vigour.

clue.text: Stumbled on hiker tackling the mountain?

definitions.text: Stumbled on hiker tackling the mountain?

indicators.note: in an across clue, the first piece is placed on, before, the second

parts.note: fell means stumbled to the ground
a walker is a hiker

explanation.surface: Someone trips over a rambler on a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: Fell is also a northern English word for a mountain or hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A hill-walker in England's north, who rambles over upland moors.

clue.text: Hail attracted attention at sea

definitions.meaning: the shout sailors give to catch another vessel's notice

explanation.surface: A hailstorm drew notice out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' reads as ice falling; it is a call.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's cry to hail a ship.
